title: Gold Coast Colony
capsule: The Gold Coast Colony was a British Crown colony in West Africa, formalized in its mature form in 1874 and expanded in 1902 to incorporate the Ashanti region (following the Fourth Anglo-Ashanti War of 1900) and the Northern Territories protectorate. It was one of the most economically productive British African colonies, exporting cocoa (the world's leading producer by the 1910s), gold, and timber through the port of Accra. Under Governor Charles Arden-Clarke and nationalist leader Kwame Nkrumah, the colony moved rapidly toward self-government: Nkrumah's Convention People's Party won elections in 1951, Nkrumah became prime minister, and on 6 March 1957 the Gold Coast became Ghana — the first sub-Saharan African colony to achieve independence in the post-war era.
